To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
YidC, a homologue of mitochondrial inner membrane Oxa1p is a component of Sec translocase in E.coli.
YidC functions as a component of the E. coli inner membrane translocating apparatus and that it is involved in the integration of hydrophobic signal anchor sequences.

YidC is a new component of the SecYEG inner‐membrane translocase that interacts with the SecYEG translocase and the hydrophobic sequences of inner membrane proteins during the insertion of these proteins into the membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of membrane protein insertion into the Escherichiacoli inner membrane.
the molecular basis of protein targeting and insertion into the Escherichcia coli inner membrane.
the molecular mechanism by which proteins are inserted into membranes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the translocase is a complex of SecA, YidC, SecY, SecE and SecG.
the YidC protein is a novel component of the E. coli Sec translocase, which is responsible for the insertion of hydrophilic signal sequences into the lipid phase of the membrane.
YidC functions in the insertion of membrane proteins in a pathway distinct from that used for secreted proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
YidC functions at the SecA/SecY interface to mediate the insertion of hydrophilic and hydrophobic sequences.
YidC functions at a late stage of the translocational process.

the Escherichiacoli YidC protein is a component of a protein‐conducting channel that is involved in the translocation of hydrophobic segments of inner membrane and secretory proteins across the cytoplasmic membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the YidC protein has a role in the biogenesis of both inner membrane and secretory proteins.
there is a second protein‐specific insertion machinery in the inner membrane of Escherichia colithat functions in conjunction with the core Sec translocase.
the SecYEG translocase is a complex of proteins, not just SecY and SecE.
